statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6473 (PostgreSQL server undersizes allocations, via integer wraparound) in 16.14 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6473/ lists 16.14 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.14 are affected), and the 16.14 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.14/, list this CVE. The fix is a series of commits on the REL_16_STABLE branch tagged Security: CVE-2026-6473, all in the REL_16_14 release tag and not in REL_16_13, among them https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/cfb610eaa02583fad12558af2eb36dab015cef02 (overflow-safe palloc_array()), https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/e24fb3247644a9baef72758806d83ec59d914781 (array_agg()), https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/a4f089c79b3f7c1790d400ec72a9258d55165dbf (regular expressions), https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5919e0005b6f23292450a44f1db5c6b2e2bb0ddf (ts_headline()) and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/6b6b26fdecc8a8e0b57ab9f0e8a6ad6212ccba36 and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5c1069c35b49227f955735ea5f2a2ee1c9c48a63 (the ltree and intarray extensions). The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 16.14-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/56de254843f841a99aedea4953a2dc9ec9338eb4/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, differs from the 16.13-r0 one only in the version, the tarball checksum and the secfixes comment, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6473 under its 16.14-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, and the ltree and intarray modules (/usr/lib/postgresql16/ltree.so and _int.so in the postgresql16-contrib package) in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-28, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.13 and is affected, while 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. As a check, the server binary contains the exact error messages these commits add, 'array size exceeds the maximum allowed (%zu)' and 'invalid memory allocation request size %zu * %zu', in 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 on both architectures and not in 16.13-r0 (16.13-r0 has only the older 'array size exceeds the maximum allowed (%d)', which the later builds also keep), and ltree.so and _int.so gain 'lquery level is too large' and 'query_int expression is too complex' at 16.14-r0 in the same way. 16.14-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6473, integer wraparound in several server features that undersizes an allocation and writes out of bounds, in 17.10. Within major version 17, releases before 17.10 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6473/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.10/. Debian's postgresql-17 17.10-0+deb13u1 upload packages PostgreSQL 17.10, and its changelog entry lists CVE-2026-6473 (https://metadata.ftp-master.debian.org/changelogs//main/p/postgresql-17/postgresql-17_17.12-0+deb13u1_changelog). The Debian tracker records the trixie fix at the later 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6473. The fixed version is this owner's rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.10 and is no longer in the repository. It is the boundary, rather than the lowest build published now, because this assessment's evidence includes that build and it carries the fix; a later boundary would list it as affected. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64.
